attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own Substack post, presented as his view.

semantics.note: 'To their peril' says the missing classical world model harms LLMs. Reading it as a causal claim fits the words. The claim has no horizon or quantifier that was dropped.

contract.note: Following the post, the contract reads 'classical world models' as explicit entity-and-state structures. It does not require every failure to come from that cause. That is an ordinary reading. Requiring controlled comparisons is fair for a causal claim.

evidence.note: The 2023 LLM+P study shows that adding formal PDDL problem descriptions plus a classical planner improves planning. That bundles state representation with search, so the gain cannot be credited to the world model alone.

reviews.rationale: The only item is a bundled comparison that adds both a formal representation and an external planner. It does not separate the effect of a missing explicit world model from the effect of search. The packet has no ablation on the relevant LLMs, and nothing contradicts the claim. The evidence does not settle the causal claim.

attribution.note: Marcus's own conclusion in his own post.

semantics.note: The drafter keeps both the unreliable play and the 'precisely because' cause. Leaving out 'can approximate' does not change what Marcus committed to.

contract.note: Limiting the claim to the ChatGPT versions discussed at publication, and requiring evidence that isolates the mechanism, is fair. Defining 'proper' as functionally adequate is an ordinary reading.

evidence.note: This 2023 behavioural study of an earlier ChatGPT points to attention limits, with partial relief from repetition. It also notes some capacity to internalise rules. It covers a different version and does not isolate the cause Marcus asserts.
This 2022 study of other transformer models shows that state tracking depends on full attention to the game history. It is about different models and is useful only for method.

reviews.rationale: Neither item measures internal representations in the 2025 ChatGPT versions or intervenes to isolate their effect. e1 hints at competing explanations (attention, self-regulation) but tests an earlier version and cannot settle the cause. The question remains unresolved.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: The drafter keeps 'much of what ails them' and the design-choice cause. The 'astonishing' remark is rightly left out as rhetoric.

contract.note: 'Much' has no threshold and the set of failures is undefined, so the reading of 'substantial share' decides the outcome. The contract says so openly. The reading is ordinary and not stretched for or against Marcus.

evidence.note: This 2023 planning study adds PDDL models together with validation feedback and external planners. The components are bundled, the study covers planning only, and it does not estimate what share of failures the missing model causes.

This Rubik's Cube study (v2 dated 2026-08-29, before the cutoff) tests explicit state-prediction objectives in experimental transformers. It is a different intervention and population from the post's LLMs.

reviews.rationale: No item estimates the share of LLM failures caused by the lack of explicit world models across failure types. e1 bundles several interventions within one domain, and e2 concerns training objectives in toy transformers. The evidence neither supports nor contradicts the claim.

attribution.note: Marcus states the incident as fact in his own post.

semantics.note: The proposition keeps the recent loss to the Atari 2600. Leaving the parenthetical hardware details and price out of scoring is reasonable.

contract.note: Reading 'Atari 2600' to include its chess software under emulation, and counting a concession as a win, are ordinary readings. Both are flagged as qualifications. The June 2025 window matches 'not long ago'.

evidence.note: The organizer's firsthand LinkedIn account says ChatGPT conceded to Atari Video Chess running in the Stella emulator, after heavy corrections.
Tom's Hardware, 9 June 2025, places the encounter on the preceding weekend and identifies the model as ChatGPT 4o. It repeats the same testimony rather than replicating the game.

reviews.rationale: The organizer's contemporaneous account (e2) records ChatGPT conceding to Atari 2600 chess software, and e3 dates the game to early June 2025, before the post. The packet contains no contradicting record. Two caveats remain: the game ran on an emulator, not original hardware, and there is no full move record. Neither defeats the plain reading.
